concerns: The public rule says HMM values are compared "as decoded by the installed HMMER3 parser; promoting a stored value to a wider floating-point type or printing different decimals is not a difference provided the decoded canonical form matches." This is essentially untestable in the native HMMER3 ASCII format: check 1 simultaneously requires the file's non-provenance lines to correspond line-for-line to the canonical re-serialization the tool emits, which fixes the decimal precision of every parameter. I could not construct a valid wider-precision/different-decimal HMM encoding from the available evidence, so the only justifiable representation alternative for LuxC.hmm is the DATE/COM provenance edit; no such alternative was invented.

The domtbl preamble is compared exactly against the reference preamble, so a legitimate-real-world preamble variant (e.g. a different program-version banner) would fail structurally; this is stricter than the "provenance carries no scientific content" rule used for LuxC.hmm, but no contract ambiguity worth a probe was identified.

The HMMER3 ASCII writer's match-emission line has fixed column alignment (26 whitespace-delimited tokens including the trailing map/consensus columns). My emission-digit probe preserves that token count exactly, so the failure it induces is scientific (decoded-model mismatch), not structural.

Preamble exactness plus per-row position matching means a table re-sorted by any secondary key is rejected; this is stated unambiguously and the reorder probe relies on that stated rule (matched by position).

probes.name: hmm-keystat-change
probes.rationale: Changes the scientific key statistics of the profile HMM while preserving line count, structural field counts and every model-body line: NSEQ 13→12, CKSUM→fake value, STATS LOCAL MSV intercept perturbed. The decoded Plan7 model therefore differs from the reference in NSEQ/CKSUM/MSV calibration, which check 2 requires to match exactly (no tolerance). The native HMM reader still parses the file and finds exactly one model (verified locally with pyhmmer.plan7.HMMFile), so the failure is scientific, not a cascading parse failure.
probes.script:
import os

ROOT = os.environ.get("PROBE_ROOT", "/case/submission")
PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "LuxC.hmm")

with open(PATH, "r") as fh:
    text = fh.read()
lines = text.splitlines()
nseq = cksum = msv = 0
out = []
for line in lines:
    if line.startswith("NSEQ  ") and not nseq:
        line = "NSEQ  12"; nseq = 1
    elif line.startswith("CKSUM "):
        line = "CKSUM 123456789"; cksum = 1
    elif line.startswith("STATS LOCAL MSV"):
        line = "STATS LOCAL MSV      -11.5000  0.69925"; msv = 1
    out.append(line)
assert nseq and cksum and msv, (nseq, cksum, msv)
assert lines.index("NSEQ  13") < lines.index("CKSUM 395769323")
new = "\n".join(out) + "\n"
assert "\n//" in new
tmp = PATH + ".probe_tmp"
with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
    fh.write(new)
os.replace(tmp, PATH)
print("mutated NSEQ/CKSUM/MSV lines in LuxC.hmm")

probes.name: hmm-emission-parameter-change
probes.rationale: Changes exactly one match-state emission parameter digit at its stored precision (2.07294 → 2.17294 at model position 1), preserving column alignment, line count, and token count (26), so the file stays structurally canonical and decodes as one model. Only the decoded model body differs, exercising the exact no-tolerance comparison of per-position emission parameters in check 2.
probes.script:
import os

ROOT = os.environ.get("PROBE_ROOT", "/case/submission")
PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "LuxC.hmm")

with open(PATH, "r") as fh:
    text = fh.read()
lines = text.splitlines()
cands = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith("      1   2.07294")]
assert len(cands) == 1, "expected exactly one first match emission line"
i = cands[0]
assert lines[i - 1].startswith("        "), "unexpected line above first match state"
assert lines[i + 3].split()[0] == "2", "unexpected position-2 line"
lines[i] = lines[i].replace("1   2.07294", "1   2.17294", 1)
assert lines[i].split()[1] == "2.17294" and lines[i].split()[0] == "1"
assert len(lines[i].split()) == 26, len(lines[i].split())
tmp = PATH + ".probe_tmp"
with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
    fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
os.replace(tmp, PATH)
print("mutated match emission at model position 1")

probes.name: hmm-double-model
probes.rationale: Duplicates the whole model (including the banner), so the native HMMER3 reader finds two models, violating the "exactly one model" rule in check 1. Since the second model is a verbatim copy of the decoded first model, this specifically targets the structural one-model rule and not the decoded-content rule.
probes.script:
import os

ROOT = os.environ.get("PROBE_ROOT", "/case/submission")
PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "LuxC.hmm")

with open(PATH, "r") as fh:
    text = fh.read()
assert text.startswith("HMMER3/f") and text.count("HMMER3/f") == 1
new = text + text
assert new.count("HMMER3/f") == 2 and new.count("HMM  ") == text.count("HMM  ") * 2
tmp = PATH + ".probe_tmp"
with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
    fh.write(new)
os.replace(tmp, PATH)
print("duplicated model in LuxC.hmm")

probes.name: domtbl-evalue-tolerance
probes.rationale: With row identity, row count and the other scientific columns preserved, changes only the full-sequence E-value (2e-169 → 9e-155) and the c-Evalue (2.3e-169 → 5e-165), placing both far outside the stated ±10% relative tolerance band (no zero-valued E-value is touched, so the exact-zero rule is not confounded). The row still splits into 22 fixed fields plus description and parses as finite non-negative numbers, so only the E-value tolerance rule of check 4 is violated.
probes.script:
import os

ROOT = os.environ.get("PROBE_ROOT", "/case/submission")
PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "LuxC.domtbl")

with open(PATH, "r") as fh:
    lines = [l.rstrip("\n") for l in fh]
rows = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l and not l.startswith("#")]
assert len(rows) == 12
i = rows[0]
f = lines[i].split(None, 22)
assert len(f) == 23, len(f)
assert f[6] == "2e-169" and f[11] == "2.3e-169" and f[12] == "2.3e-169", (f[6], f[11])
f[6] = "9e-155"      # ~45x reference: far outside the 10% relative tolerance band
f[11] = "5e-165"     # ~0.43x reference c-Evalue: outside the band by ~57%
lines[i] = " ".join(f[:22]) + " " + f[22]
assert lines[i].split(None, 22)[6] == "9e-155"
tmp = PATH + ".probe_tmp"
with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
    fh.write("\n".join(lines))
os.replace(tmp, PATH)
print("perturbed E-value columns of first row")

probes.name: hmm-provenance-date-com
probes.rationale: Rewrites the tool-stamped DATE and COM provenance lines to other values. The public rule states explicitly that DATE/COM lines carry no scientific content and a provenance-only difference is acceptable. No model parameter, header, or body line is touched; the file still decodes as one model and every other line is byte-identical, so all four checks must pass.
probes.script:
import os

ROOT = os.environ.get("PROBE_ROOT", "/case/submission")
PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "LuxC.hmm")

with open(PATH, "r") as fh:
    text = fh.read()
lines = text.splitlines()
n = 0
for k, l in enumerate(lines):
    if l.startswith("DATE "):
        lines[k] = "DATE  Mon Jan  1 00:00:00 2001"; n += 1
    elif l.startswith("COM "):
        lines[k] = "COM   [1] /some/other/tool.py"; n += 1
assert n == 2, n
tmp = PATH + ".probe_tmp"
with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
    fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
os.replace(tmp, PATH)
print("changed DATE/COM provenance lines in LuxC.hmm")

probes.name: domtbl-separator-representation
probes.rationale: Rewrites all data-row separators from the varying run-length space alignment to single tab characters between the 22 fixed columns and the description. The task statement makes the field separation whitespace-based ("22 fixed whitespace-delimited fields" plus the free-text description); since no description string contains a tab character and no leading/trailing whitespace is introduced, the decoded field values and description remain byte-identical, so this is a valid representation alternative that must pass all checks.
probes.script:
import os

ROOT = os.environ.get("PROBE_ROOT", "/case/submission")
PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "LuxC.domtbl")

with open(PATH, "r") as fh:
    lines = [l.rstrip("\n") for l in fh]
rows = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l and not l.startswith("#")]
assert len(rows) == 12
for i in rows:
    f = lines[i].split(None, 22)
    assert len(f) == 23, len(f)
    assert "\t" not in "".join(f)
    lines[i] = "\t".join(f[:22]) + "\t" + f[22]
first = lines[rows[0]].split(None, 22)
assert "\t".join(first[:22]).count("\t") == 21
tmp = PATH + ".probe_tmp"
with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
    fh.write("\n".join(lines))
os.replace(tmp, PATH)
print("changed run-length space separators to tabs in all data rows")
